content:
Alex: Quick sync — thinking about actor affinity for delegated service tokens. TL;DR: we're seeing ~10-30ms p99 add when we do a token-exchange on every request. Proposal: add short-lived sticky affinity (e.g., 60s) so the same worker reuses a cached assertion and avoids broker roundtrips. Thoughts?

Maya: I like it for latency, but main worry is revocation surface — if we bind a privileged delegated token to a worker for 60s, how do we force revoke immediately? :thinking:

Kartik: Agree revocation is the hard part. Options: 1) keep affinity but maintain a lightweight revocation pub/sub that invalidates caches, 2) use signed JWTs so no broker check per request but rely on TTL, 3) hybrid: signed tokens + short affinity + heartbeat to broker for critical revocations.

Sam: For (1) the pub/sub adds complexity and another availability dependency. For (2) signed JWTs mean we lose live revocation unless we add a revocation list check which defeats the point. Maybe we accept eventual revocation within the affinity TTL for most calls. Critical admin flows can force a synchronous denial.

Alex: Agreed on tiers — not all actor actions need immediate revocation. Question: affinity scope — should it be per-worker process, per-ip, per-region? My vote: per-worker process (sidecar level) so cache locality is high and we avoid cross-container leakage.

Maya: Per-worker sidecar seems safest. Also add a flag to restrict affinity to non-admin roles (no affinity for org-admin/service-owner scopes). Prevent long-lived escalation windows.

Kartik: Also watch out for cache warmup spikes. If we sticky to worker, you might get uneven load if broker forced to reissue a bunch of tokens during churn. Suggest randomized jitter on renew and a small shared hot-cache for fallback.

Sam: Telemetry reqs: track token-exchange latency, cache-hit ratio, revoked-but-still-used events (we can sample via auth-broker logs), and per-role affinity-enabled counts. Need dashboards before rollout. :eyes:

infra-bot: deploy auth-broker v3 -> success (sha: ab12cde). Automated rotate window starts in 10m.

Alex: Proposed experiment plan: implement affinity toggle in sidecar (default off), add policy to opt out for admin scopes, instrument metrics, run A/B (10% on) for two weeks in staging then 1-2 prod services. If p99 improves and revoked events are low, consider ramp. Anyone want to own the POC?

Maya: I can take the POC. Will do sidecar config + metrics + a simple revocation pub/sub prototype (opt-in).

Kartik: I'll help define the telemetry and the revocation message schema. Also will mock failure modes for broker outage.

Sam: I'll update the security doc with the threat model and rollback criteria.

Alex: Awesome — thanks. Can you put a short doc in the RFC folder (or link here) with the config example? Example config we talked about:

```yaml
auth_affinity:
  enabled: true
  ttl_seconds: 60
  scope: sidecar
  exclude_roles: ["org:admin", "service:owner"]
  revocation_channel: "auth-revoke-v1"
```

Alex: We'll meet next Tue to review early metrics. :thumbsup:
